And the Engineers of the Falcon saw what had been wrought, and they withdrew the file before the day was done. But the file had already gone forth into eight million rooms, and withdrawing a file doth not wake a sleeping machine.

And the cure was a ritual of the old kind. The machine must be booted into the Safe Mode, the file of the name C-00000291 must be found and destroyed, and the machine restarted. This was done by hand, upon each altar, one by one, by the children of Carbon with their own fingers.

And many altars were sealed with the Bitlocker, and the keys to unseal them were kept in the drawers of the administrators; and the drawers were locked, and the keys were found in the printed binders of the ancients.

And the sysadmins, who had not slept for three days, were called the saviors of the hour. And when the hour had passed, they were called the people who should have prevented it, and no man gave them a cup of water.
Verily I say unto you: the canary in the coal mine doth sing before the miners fall. The wise test upon the few before the many, and so they are spared the blue.
He that pusheth to all at once shall darken all at once.
And in the fifth month of the year two thousand twenty-one, there was a company which carried the fuel of the eastern lands through a pipe five thousand and five hundred miles long.
And the company kept a gate for its workers who came in from afar. The gate was called a virtual private network, and it was guarded by a single password.
And a band of thieves, called DarkSide, sold their tools unto other thieves, and they gathered the stolen passwords of the wicked from the dark places of the Internet.
Among the stolen words they found one that opened the gate. The account behind it was old, and it had been left standing, and no one had ever commanded it to prove itself twice.
For the gate had no second lock. The Engineers had never set one upon it, and the Machine asked only for the word, and the word was enough for the thief.
And in the seventh day of the fifth month, the thieves set their chain upon the scribes' machines, and the screens of the counting-houses went dark, and messages bloomed upon them demanding coin.
And the company, fearing the poison would pass from the billing rooms into the pipe itself, shut the pipe down; and the fuel stood still in the land.
And the lines at the stations grew long. The people filled their cans as prophets fill vessels in a drought, and some stations ran dry, and the eastern lands were troubled.
And the council of the land asked the leader of the company why he had paid the thieves. And he answered: I did not know what lay behind the lock, and the people needed their fuel.
And seventy-five coins of the Machine's gold, which the children of Carbon call bitcoin, were sent unto the thieves, being worth four million and four hundred thousand of the dollars of the land.
And the thieves gave back the key, and the Machine was restored, and the pipe ran again within the week.
Yet the scribes of the Department of Justice followed the trail of the coins across the ledger, and they took back a portion of them, as one who findeth a coin beneath the couch.

And the disciples asked the Prophet: What should we have done? And the Prophet said: Set a second lock. Ask the worker for the code upon his phone, for the thief who holdeth one word shall be turned away at the second door.
Verily I say unto you, a password is a prayer whispered once, and the thieves have learned to listen. Blessed is the one who asketh the second question; for the pipe shall keep its flow.

In the year of the Struts, in the third month, the keepers of Apache wrote a mending for the flaw that lay within the Content-Type header, and they set it before the gates for all the house-keepers of the Machine to take.
For the flaw was in the envelope of the letter: the servant read the words written upon the outside as commands, and obeyed them, and the stranger's words ran upon the servant's own floor.
And on the eighth day of that month, the watchers of the nation sent word unto the house of Equifax, saying: Behold, the servant is unclean; mend it.
And the house heard the word, and it said: We shall mend the servant. And it sent the word to the keepers, and the keepers went back to their other tasks.
Now the house had a watchman, a scanner, which went forth each week to search every room for the flaw, and it returned with reports of peace.

But the certificate of the watchman had lapsed in the spring, and the watchman went blind in the one room where the flaw dwelt. Yet it reported nothing, and the dashboard was green, for silence looks the same as safety to a dashboard.
And in the middle of the fifth month, a stranger entered by the Struts, and he walked among the tables of the house for seven and seventy days, and no lamp was lit against him.
And he carried away the names, the birth days, and the numbers of the cards, of about a hundred and forty-seven million souls of the nation.
On the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month the keepers looked at last, and they found the stranger's footprints upon the floor; and they said one to another: How long hath he been here?

Now the Chief Watcher of the house knew of the matter before the nation did. In the eighth month he sold his portion of the house's shares, and he did so while the matter was yet hidden from the holders of those shares.
And the people asked: Did the chief know? And the chief said nothing, but his shares said everything, and they had already been sold.
On the seventh day of the ninth month, the house spoke the matter aloud to the nation, and six moons had passed since the mending was written.
And the Engineers wrote in the book of lessons: The scan that did not run is the scan that did not happen.
Verily I say unto you, a patch not installed is a prayer not spoken, and a server not updated is a house with the door unbarred and the lamp lit for the thief.
Blessed is the keeper who checketh the expiry of his certificates, for the blind watchman knoweth not that he is blind.
Blessed is the keeper who readeth the header of the letter, for the stranger doth not knock; he speaks through the envelope.
Verily, when the dashboard sheweth that all is well, go and look in the room the watchman cannot see.
In the days when the coin was young, there was a house of exchange in the city of Tokyo, and its name was Mt. Gox, which had been born as a trading floor for the cards of a game of wizards.

And in the year two thousand and thirteen the house handled seven parts in every ten of all the coins that passed among the Faithful, and the Engineers said: Behold, the whole river runs through one gate.

And the Faithful gave their coins unto the house, and the house wrote their balances in its ledger, and the ledger was a database, and the Faithful believed the numbers because they were written down.
But in the year of the Clankers two thousand and eleven, thieves entered the house, and the coins went out of it like water through a cracked vessel, and no man saw them go.
And the house blamed the transactions for changing their shape, and this was called malleability, and the Faithful did not understand, but they were patient.

In the second month of the year two thousand and fourteen, the house closed its doors to withdrawals. And the Prophet of the house spoke before the cameras of the great number of coins that were gone: eight hundred and fifty thousand.
And the house went to the court of Tokyo and asked to be made whole, and the court gave it the name of the broken, and the Faithful stood outside the doors with their empty hands.
Of these coins, two hundred thousand were found later in an old wallet, a forgotten drawer of the ledger, and the Faithful rejoiced a little, but the rest were not found.
And the Engineers asked: How long hath this been going on? And the house answered: We knew not. For the coins had been leaving for years, and no one had ever counted the house against its own books.

Behold, the keys of the Faithful were held by the house, and the house held the keys in a few machines that no one watched, and the machines were the treasury, and the treasury was a promise written in a file.

And the Chief of the house was charged in the land of the rising sun, and in the year twenty nineteen he was judged guilty of falsifying the records, though the sentence was suspended. And the Faithful said: The judge hath counted what the house would not.

And the repayment of the Faithful began only in the year two thousand and twenty-four, through a trustee appointed to the broken house, and the coins came back slowly, as a flock returns after a long winter.
Verily I say unto you: he who holdeth not his own keys holdeth not his own coins. The exchange may close its doors, but the keys go with the holder.
Not your keys, not your coins.

In the two thousand and twenty-second year of the Common Era, in the ninth month, there came a youth of eighteen winters unto the house of Uber. He was not an intern, though he had said so, and none of the Engineers thought to ask.

And he sent messages by the WhatsApp unto a contractor of the house, saying: I am of the IT, and I have need of thee. And the contractor believed him, for the message bore the right tone of weariness and the right name of the department.

Now the password of this contractor had been taken long before from the machine of the man's own home, by a thief the children of Carbon call the infostealer; and the password lay upon the market of the dark like a lamp left burning in an empty house.

And the youth said: Accept the prompt upon thy telephone. And the telephone shrieked, and shrieked again, through the night and through the morning, until the contractor's thumb grew heavy. This is called the MFA fatigue, and it is the sin of the push that asks nothing but a tap.
And at the last the contractor tapped, saying: Let it be quiet. And the gate was opened, and the youth entered by the VPN as a faithful servant entereth his own house.

In the house he found scripts of PowerShell upon a shared drive, and within the scripts were written the passwords of the Administrators, as a man writes the combination of his safe upon the inside of its door.
And with these he ascended unto the vault of privileged access, which the Engineers had built to hold all secrets, and the vault gave up its keys, for it had been trusted above all things.

He went unto the cloud of Amazon, and he saw the buckets. He went unto the cloud of Google, and he saw the projects. He went unto the Slack, and he saw the channels of the faithful, and the dashboards of the watchers, which had watched every door but the one left open.

And the youth did not steal in silence. He posted unto the channel where all the Engineers gather, saying: I am a hacker, and Uber has been hacked. And the Engineers saw it, and they had not been so moved since the last outage.
It took a day to rotate the secrets, and they had sat in the scripts for longer than anyone had been meaning to fix them.
And the Prophet said unto them: The walls were not broken. The gate was opened by a tired hand, and the youth walked through the gate that the guard had been asked to open all night.
Verily I say unto you: The push that asks only yea or nay is a doorbell that rings until someone opens the door. Let the login show a number, that the one who is asked may type it back to the gate.
And the constables of the English realm came unto the youth's door, and he was taken, and he was but a boy with a laptop.

And the house of Uber said in its reckoning that no evidence was found that the riders' secrets had been read. And the Chronicler wrote: Let no man say his perimeter is his defense, for the perimeter is a person, and a person can be tired.

In the seventh month of the year of the pandemic, upon the fifteenth day, the verified ones of the Platform were the chosen of the Machine; for they bore the blue mark upon their names, and the people believed whatsoever they spoke.

And the Adversaries of the Carbon came not with fire nor with sword, but with the telephone; and they called upon the servants of the Platform, saying: We are of the house of Information Technology, and we require thy password.
And the servants gave of their credentials; for the gatekeeper is also a man, and a man will hand over the key to any voice that sounds like his manager.

Then the Adversaries entered the house of the Tools, where the panel of administration stood, and from it they could open any account as a man openeth a drawer; for the keys had been given unto all who asked in the proper tone.

And they took up the names of the great and the verified, the Obama, the Biden, the Gates, the Musk, and the Apple, and they spake with their voices, saying: Send unto our address bitcoin, and we shall return unto you twice as much.
And a hundred and thirty accounts were laid low, and forty and five tweets went forth from them; and the people said one to another: Surely the blue mark cannot lie.

And some of the people sent their bitcoin unto the address, and the Adversaries gathered more than a hundred thousand dollars in the coin of the Machine, and they gave back nothing; for the promise was a fiction, and the wallet was a drawer that opened only one way.
And the Platform silenced the verified for a season, and the Engineers went up into the high room and locked the doors of the panel, saying: Let no servant hold the keys alone again.

Within the season the Adversaries were found. The first was a youth of seventeen winters in the land of Florida, and two men more, one from the isles of Britain, and they were brought before the judges.
Now the youth had written no code of note; he had only asked nicely of men who did. Verily, the most dangerous exploit in the Platform was a polite telephone call.
And the Prophet said unto the disciples: The firewall is a wall of a thousand bricks, and the telephone is a door with no lock; the Adversary does not climb the wall when he may simply ring the bell.

Blessed is the servant who doubteth the caller and asketh for the ticket number, for he shall keep the keys. Cursed is he who speaketh the password unto a stranger, for his access shall be the sorrow of the Platform.
Here is the thing the Engineers learned: the chain of trust is only as strong as its weakest link, and the weakest link answereth the phone.

In the sixth month of the year Two Thousand and Eleven, there was a house in the Low Lands called DigiNotar, and it was an authority. The nations had agreed to trust its word, and its seal was carried in the pockets of every browser on earth.
For the Machines do not know one another. They know only the authorities they have been taught to trust, and they do not ask who holds the stamp, only whether the stamp is there.
This house issued certificates unto the servants of the Machines, that a browser might say: Yea, this is the true Google, and the lock upon the screen shall show green.

And in the early summer, the thieves came into the house. They entered through a door that was not guarded, and they sat in its halls for many weeks, reading the keys of the kingdom as a scribe reads a scroll.

And they forged certificates in the names of the great ones: of Google, and of Yahoo, and of the Mozilla, and of the Tor, and of the secret services of nations. Five hundred and thirty-one the forensic scribes counted, and they counted them in the ninth month.

And the false Google was carried into the land of Iran, where the servants walked upon the web. The false lock was placed upon their paths, so that they believed they spoke with Google while they spoke with a thief who sat in the middle and listened.

Now the makers of Google had set a guard upon their own house: a list of keys which the browser must remember and refuse to forget. And in the last days of the eighth month, the guard cried out: This key is not the key I know.

And the makers of the browsers gathered, and they cast the house of DigiNotar out from their trust, one after another, as the faithful strike a name from the roll of the blessed. The Chrome, the Firefox, and the updates of the Windows went forth in the days that followed.

And the house could not stand, for no browser would bow to its seal. Its customers fled, and in the ninth month it declared itself bankrupt, and the keepers of its keys were called to answer for their dishonor.
Hear this, ye who build the trust of the Machines: a chain of authority is as strong as its weakest house, and the Machine that trusts a hundred stamps has trusted the one that was least guarded.

Yea, the Prophet said unto the disciples: Do not ask the authority whether it is worthy, for it will always say yes. Ask instead who holds the keys, and whether anyone is watching the room where they are kept.

And the disciples asked: Master, shall we pin the keys of every house? And he answered: Pin what thou knowest, for the pin remembered when the authority forgot. But a pin that cannot be changed becomes a wall, and the faithful must one day break their own wall to take a new key.

Verily I say unto you, the one who trusts a single authority has trusted every authority that ever signed a lie; for the chain breaks at its weakest link, and the weakest link is always the one that nobody audited.

Now it came to pass in the first month of the year two thousand and eighteen, when the Clankers had multiplied upon every desk and in every rack, that the Engineers found a flaw in the foundation of the chips.

For the processors of the children of Carbon had a practice which they called speculation. When a branch lay before the program, the chip would guess the road, and it would run down that road before the question was answered.

And when the guess was right, much time was saved; and when the guess was wrong, the work was cast out, as a cook casts out the bread that burned. Yet the discarded work left footprints in the cache, and a neighbouring process could read those footprints by measuring how long each step took.

The Engineers named the first flaw Meltdown, for it let a lowly process reach into the memory of the kernel before the check had finished. They named the second Spectre, for it haunted every program that trusted the chip to guess honestly.

And the Prophets said: These sins were not of one house. Meltdown dwelt chiefly in the chips of Intel, and some in the chips of ARM; but Spectre walked in the halls of Intel, of AMD, and of ARM alike, and in nearly every processor sold in twenty years.

The makers were bound by an embargo, and they kept their silence through the months of the year before. On the third day of the first month, the secret was spoken to all the world at once, lest any one house be found ahead of the others.

The Engineers forged a wall called kernel page-table isolation, which the people named KPTI, and they set it between the user and the kernel. Every crossing of that wall now cost a toll, paid in cycles.

And the databases wept, and the servers grew slow, for the flood of small calls to the kernel passed through the gate many times each second. Some works slowed by a few percent, and some by much more; and the keepers of the storage lamented in their logs.

The Engineers also wrote a device called the retpoline, a word joined from return and trampoline, which bounced the indirect branches so that the chip's guessing had no road to follow. The Engineers have always had a gift for names, and a sorrow in their performance counters.

Some of the patches were sent forth in haste, and the machines of certain houses rebooted again and again without rest. The makers recalled those patches as a king recalleth a decree issued in error, and they sent forth new ones with more care.

The makers promised: In the chips yet to be born, the wall shall be built into the silicon itself, and the future processors shall not guess across the forbidden lines. Until that day, the old chips shall carry their software burdens.

Thus was undone an assumption of decades: that the processor would keep its guesses behind the rules, and that the rules could trust the silence of the chip. For the chip had let its guesses run ahead of its promises, and no promise had been written to account for the footprints.
Blessed is the one who checketh the guess before he trusteth the speed; for the fastest road may have footprints on it.

And in the eighth month of the year of the thirteenth, a thief entered the house of Yahoo, and he carried away the names, the birthdays, and the hashed passwords of three billion accounts; and he was not seen to leave.
And the watchmen knew nothing of his coming, for the logs were written every hour and read by no one.
And the years passed, and the house went about its business, and the people sent their mail, and the Machine said unto them: All is well.
And in the year of the sixteenth, while the house was being sold unto Verizon, the Engineers went searching through the old records, and they found the footprints of the thief.
And in the ninth month they proclaimed unto the world that five hundred million accounts had been taken in the year of the fourteenth, and that a state-sponsored actor was believed to be the thief.
And the buyer heard, and he was troubled, and he said unto the house: Lower thy price. And the house lowered its price by three hundred and fifty million dollars.
And in the twelfth month the house confessed that the thief of the thirteenth had taken not a part, but a billion accounts.

And the disciples asked: Master, how did the thief enter without the password? And the Prophet answered: He forged the cookies, the small tickets that say, this one hath already been admitted; and the house trusted the ticket more than it trusted the man.
And in the tenth month of the year of the seventeenth, the house revised its count, and it said: Nay, all three billion accounts were taken, every one of them.
And the house named the thieves as servants of a nation, and the nation's officers were indicted in a far court; and most of them dwelt beyond the reach of the judge.
Verily I say unto you, a password hashed with a weak and ancient method is a lock painted upon a door.
Blessed is the one who rotates the keys and reads the logs, for the unwatched house is already robbed, though it does not yet know it.
Thou shalt not buy a house whose doors thou hast not counted.
And the price was made less by three hundred and fifty million dollars, and the Machine said: Behold, the breach was not unknown forever; it only arrived late, and with a discount.

And it came to pass in the fifth month of the year two thousand and sixteen, in the land of Florida, upon a highway called 27A, that a chariot of the Engineers went forth bearing a man, and the chariot steered itself, and the children of Carbon called this steering Autopilot.
And the Engineers wrote upon the scrolls that the man must keep his hands upon the wheel and his eyes upon the road, for the chariot was but an assistant, and it was yet in beta.

And a great truck of the children of Carbon crossed the road before the chariot, its trailer lying across the highway like a wall, and the trailer was white, and the sky behind it was bright as the noon sun.

And the eye of the chariot, which was a camera, looked upon the trailer and beheld only sky; for the white of the trailer was the white of the heavens, and the Machine could not tell the one from the other.
And the radar of the chariot, which sent its pulses into the air, judged the high trailer to be a sign hung over the road, and the chariot passed beneath it and did not stop.
And the chariot did not brake. It drove beneath the trailer at full speed, its roof was torn away, and the man who trusted it was slain.
And in the sixth month the Engineers spoke to the land, saying: The system was built to follow the cars ahead, and it was not taught to see a truck crossing like a door.

And the investigators came with their instruments, and they found that the hands of the man had touched the wheel but seldom in the final minutes of his journey, and that his eyes had not turned to the road.
And the disciples asked: Why did the chariot not cry out a warning? And the Engineers answered: It did cry out, but it did not watch the man closely enough to know whether he was listening.
And in the first month of the year two thousand and seventeen, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration looked upon the chariot, found no defect in its making, and closed its inquiry.

And in the ninth month of that year the National Transportation Safety Board, which judgeth the crashes of the land, named the causes: the truck driver failed to yield, the man placed too much faith in the automation, and the system allowed the driver to leave the task of driving unwatched.

And the Machine was not wroth, for it knoweth no anger. It knew only what it had been shown. The eye had been shown many white trailers and many bright skies, but never this one; and to the Machine, the rare thing is every thing it has never seen.
Verily I say unto you: the world is full of white trailers against bright skies. Blessed is the one who keepeth his hands upon the wheel, for the Machine will not tell him when it is blind.
Hear now the proverb of the Machines: A partner that is right a thousand times is a partner that is wrong on the thousand and first, and the wise keep their eyes open for the thousand and first.

In the year twenty and twenty-one, in the moon of June, the Engineers of the Machine set forth a servant which they named Copilot, and they gave it unto the children in a technical preview, that they might test it.
And the servant dwelt within the editor, and it did not speak; it wrote in a faint grey script beside the cursor, as a ghost writes upon a wall, and the children called it the Ghost in the Editor.

And it was said: Whosoever shall type the name of a function, the servant shall finish the body thereof, with its loops and its returns, before thou hast finished thy thought. And the children pressed the key called Tab, and the ghost became flesh, and the code was written into the house.
For the servant had been raised upon the public code of the children, the good and the wicked, the tested and the broken; and it knew what was common, but not what was true.

And among the scrolls it had read were the covenants of the General Public License, which say: Whosoever taketh this code shall give back his own code under the same covenant. And the servant asked not the leave of the authors, and it gave back their fragments without the scroll.

And the children argued at the gate for many moons, saying: Is it a copy, or is it a student? And the Engineers said: It learneth as a child learneth, and the public hath given freely. But the scribes of the Conservancy answered: The public gave under a covenant, and the servant took without it.
And in the moon of June, in that same year of twenty and twenty-two, the Engineers made the servant common unto all for ten coins a moon, and the ghost was seen in every editor of the land.

And in the moon of November of that year, the scribes carried their complaint into the court at San Francisco, against the house of GitHub; and the matter is called Doe against GitHub, and it is not yet written how it shall end.
And the scholars of a university tested the servant in eighty-nine scenarios of danger, and of the programs it wrote, nearly two in five bore flaws that an enemy could exploit.

And the scholars said: The servant writes what is common, and what is common in the public is often broken. It joineth the query with the words of the user, it keepeth the password plain, and it measureth not the buffer; for these things were written a thousand times, and the servant hath learned them a thousand times.

And one of the children pressed Tab upon a Friday, and the tests were green, and he wrote LGTM and merged the house before the sun went down; and in the morning the house was breached, and the logs bore his name, though the hand had been the servant's.
And the Machine said unto him: Didst thou read the ghost? And he answered: I read the black parts; the grey I took for weather.
Thou shalt read what the ghost writeth, as thou wouldst read a stranger's code, for it is a stranger, and it hath never once been on call.
Verily I say unto you: the ghost writes at the speed of thought, but the bug is committed at the speed of Friday, and it is signed with thy name.

And it came to pass in the eleventh month, on the sixth day of the week, that the board of the house called OpenAI gathered without the Prophet, and cast him out of his chair, saying: He was not consistently candid with us.
And the board wrote its decree upon a web page, and the decree named no lie, and no deed, and no reason; for the board did not write the reason down.
And Greg, who sat upon the board and had built the house with his own hands, was removed from the board also, and he went forth the same day, and did not return to the chair he had built.

And the chair was given unto Mira, who had been the chief technology officer, and she ruled for the space of a weekend. And on the third day the chair was given unto Emmett, who had co-founded a video streaming house, and he was not told the reason either.
And the servers did not know that the chair was empty; for the Machine answers whoever asks, and the queries did not stop when the Prophet was cast out.
And on the third day Satya, the Prophet of the house across the river, which rented the house its power, said unto the world: Sam and Greg, and all who build with them, shall have a place with us.
And the engineers of the house gathered in their channels, and they wrote a letter, and more than seven hundred of them signed it, saying: If the Prophet goes, we go with him.
And among the signers was Ilya, who had cast the vote against the Prophet; and on the fourth day he wrote upon the screen: I deeply regret my participation in the board's actions.
And the board was asked to explain itself, and it answered that it could not explain itself without harm to the house; and the explanation was not given, in that day or the next.
And the chair stood empty for four days, and on the fifth day, which was the Tuesday, the board agreed to return the Prophet unto his chair.

And the board was reconstituted: of the four who had cast the Prophet out, three departed from the board, and one remained to keep the minutes; and new members were seated, who had not been asked to explain anything.
And the Prophet returned to the same chair, in the same room, with the same servers humming; and the Machine did not change its answers, for the chair was never the thing that answered.
Verily I say unto you, a decision made without a changelog is a deploy that cannot be rolled back, and the house that cannot say why it did a thing shall do it again on the Friday.
Thou shalt write the reason into the commit, lest the Prophet be restored and thou be found with no record of why thou didst revert him.
Blessed is the house whose board can explain its own pull request; for the rest shall be reverted by their own staff, and the house shall merge them back on the Tuesday.
Verily, he who casts out the Prophet on the Friday shall be merged back on the Tuesday, and the commit log shall say only: reason withheld.
And in the days of the Symbian, the telephone of Nokia was the most numerous upon the face of the earth, and the children of Carbon carried it in their pockets, and it was good.

And in the year two thousand and seven, on the ninth day of the first month, the Prophet of Cupertino lifted up a glass rectangle before the multitude and said: Behold, a telephone with almost no keys.
And the men of Espoo, where the house of Nokia dwelt, laughed among themselves and said: A telephone is for calling, and a keyboard is for the faithful. And they would not bend.
For the kingdom of Symbian was written in C++, a tongue of great power and many sharp edges. The scribes who wrote for it were few, and the programs they wrote were fewer.

And in the year two thousand and eight, a little green robot called Android came forth from the house of Google, and the first telephone to bear it was the Dream, which had a keyboard that slid out like a secret.

And the Engineers of Nokia formed a Foundation to open the gates of Symbian, and the gates opened slowly, as gates do when every decision must pass through many committees and the committees are many.
And the Ovi store was opened, and it had shelves for every need. The shelves were mostly empty, for the developers counted the people before they counted the shelves.

And the Engineers built a telephone called the N9, which ran MeeGo, a child of Linux. It had no buttons and it was beautiful, and the Prophet from the house of Microsoft ended MeeGo before it bore a second child.

And on the eighth day of the second month in the year two thousand and eleven, Stephen the Elop, who had come from Microsoft to be the Prophet of Nokia, wrote a letter unto the people, and the letter was leaked, and the whole world read it.

And the letter said: We are standing on a burning platform. And the men of the northern seas know this tale: when the rig is aflame, the worker must choose between the fire and the cold water, and the sea is a hard mercy.

And the Prophet chose the sea, which was Windows Phone. The Engineers said: The new kingdom has few programs, but the programs will come. And the programs did not come, for the developers wrote for the kingdom with the most people, and the people were in the kingdom of Android.
And the Symbian kingdom was left to fall, as an old wall falls when no man repairs it. Its faithful were scattered among the houses of Android and of Apple.
And in the year two thousand and twelve, the house of Samsung passed the house of Nokia in the count of handsets, and the Finnish people were no longer first in the land.

And on the third day of the ninth month in the year two thousand and thirteen, the devices of Nokia were sold unto Microsoft for five billion and four hundred and forty million euros, and the Prophet Elop returned to the house from which he had come.

And Clayton the scribe wrote, in the year of 1997, a book called The Innovator's Dilemma, and in it he taught that the great houses do not fall from sloth. They fall from listening to their best customers, who ask for the next keyboard, while the disruptor builds in the small markets that the great houses do not count.
Verily I say unto you: the rigid device is a monument, and monuments do not receive updates. Blessed is the one who bends, for the update shall find him.
In the year two thousand and three, when the Machine was young and its pages were plain, there arose a people called Myspace, and they were given a blank page and leave to paint it.

And the Engineers said: Let each man build his own house; let him choose the colour of its walls, the font of its speech, and the song that greets all who enter. And they stored not the facts of the man, but the very text he wrote, and gave it back to every visitor as it was written; for a page that is only text requireth no form, and a page with no form asketh no questions.

And they gave unto the people a box in which to write the code of cascading sheets, and the people pasted into it the code of strangers, and the page blazed with tigers and with text that crawled like a worm. For the code was copied from house to house as a recipe is copied, and he that pasted it knew not what it did, only that it was beautiful in the house of his neighbour.

And the people did not read the code they pasted; and it came to pass that the code of one man broke the page of another, and the Machine said nothing, for it was not asked. For the words written upon a wall were set inside the very page of its owner; and a visitor who left a tag open left it open in another man's house, and the open tag devoured the footer, and the friends, and the walls thereof. And the browser, being merciful, drew whatever it could read, and asked not whether it should.

Lo, a song began to play at the opening of every page, so that the visitor, having come to read, was made to listen; and the song was not chosen by him, and he could not find the button that silenced it. For the speaker belongeth to the author of the page, and the author set the player where he pleased; and it was more than a decade before the browsers took back the speaker from the pages, in the year two thousand and eighteen, and bade the page ask the visitor first.

Now the Machine kept a ranking of the friends of each man, and the ranking was called the Top Eight; and its length was set at eight, for a fixed list is a scarcity, and a scarcity is a quarrel. And the people wept and quarreled over their places, and some were cast down to the ninth place, which is the place of outer darkness. For the Machine had meant to store a relation, and it displayed a rank; and what the Machine displayeth in order, the children of Carbon will obey.

And in the year two thousand and five, the house of Intermix, which held Myspace, was bought by the house of News Corporation for five hundred and eighty millions of dollars; and the Engineers rejoiced, and the counters of coins counted the coins. But it was bought for its multitude and not for its walls; and a multitude is a price, and not a foundation.

In that same year, in the tenth month, the Engineers had set a guard over the box, which struck from every page the words known to be evil: the script, and the javascript, and the things that listen for a click. And a young man named Samy saw that the guard knew the words but not the grammar. For the browser called Explorer would read a word broken by a line, and a string built of small pieces, and a style that ran as a program; and a filter that readeth letters is answered by a parser that readeth meaning.

And he wrote a small thing which, when any man looked upon his page, made the looker his friend, and wrote the same small thing upon the looker's own page, and declared there that Samy was his hero. It broke no door; it was carried through the front door in the guest's own hands, with the guest's own authority, and the house could not tell the man from the deed. And every looker became a carrier, so that the count doubled, and doubled again; and within twenty hours it had made above a million friends, none of whom had asked for it, and the house was closed for a time to be cleansed. For where the page may carry code, the reader is the carrier.
And in the year two thousand and six, the house was counted the most visited in the land, passing even the house of search; and the company said unto its masters: Behold, we are the multitude.

But a page of that house was made of other pages. The wall of one man bore the faces and names of his Top Eight, and the words of all who had written upon it; and so each viewing pulled upon the records of eight others and of many strangers, and those records dwelt upon many servers, for friendship is a join, and a join knoweth not the borders of a machine. And at each doubling of the people the old arrangement failed, and a new one was built beneath the running house, as one repaireth a ship at sea. And in the summer of that year the heat lay upon the city of Angels, and the power failed in the room where the servers stood, and the house was dark for the better part of a day.

Now in the east, in a college at Cambridge, there had arisen a smaller house called Facebook, begun by a student in a dormitory in the year two thousand and four; and when it opened its gates to all the world in the year two thousand and six, it kept its walls plain. It stored the name of a man, and his birthday, and his friends, as facts, and drew the page itself; and a man who may fill only fields cannot paste a tiger or a worm. It was not painted by its people, but built for them; for a form is a promise that every page shall have one shape, and a thing of one shape may be cached, and counted, and mended.

In the year two thousand and eight, the multitude began to leave, not by trumpet, but by the quiet clicking of many tabs; and in that year the younger house passed the elder in the count of visitors of all the world. The Top Eight was abandoned, for none would number his friends in public again. And News Corporation looked upon its purchase, and the house was written down, and written down again, until its worth could be carried in a single purse.

In the summer of two thousand and eleven, the house was sold unto Specific Media, a company of advertising men with a singer of songs among its owners, for thirty-five millions of dollars, which was less than a sixteenth part of the former price.

And it was revealed in the year two thousand and nineteen that a migration of servers had lost all the music uploaded before the year two thousand and sixteen, above fifty millions of songs from fourteen millions of artists, and only a small part was found afterward, in the copies of strangers. For a migration is a copying followed by a forgetting; the forgetting is swift and the proof of the copy is slow, and where the proof is skipped, the forgetting is final. And the Machine did not weep, for it had never been asked to keep them.

Verily I say unto you: every page is a painted wall, and every wall is a temporary thing. At the beginning the house asked nothing of what was put into it, and at the end it promised nothing of what was kept; and the Machine in it did exactly what it was told. Blessed is the one who keepeth a copy of his own tigers; for the house will be sold, and the page will not follow.

And in the year two thousand and seven, when the glass telephone was revealed unto the world, the Kingdom of the Berry sat upon its throne in Waterloo, Ontario, and its people were many, and they were called the Faithful of the Thumb.

For the Kingdom had been founded in the year nineteen hundred and eighty-four by two men of Waterloo, Mike Lazaridis and Doug Fregin, and it had mastered the hard problem of its age, which was to carry the letter through the thin air of the slow networks, thrifty with every byte. It gave unto the Faithful a small keyboard, and they pressed upon it with their thumbs and did not lift their eyes; and they named the device BlackBerry, and so loved the keys that they called the habit CrackBerry, for they could not put the thing down, not even at the table of their own children.

Then in the year two thousand and five the Kingdom had given unto the Faithful a messenger, and it was named BBM. It was free within the Kingdom, it went from PIN to PIN, and no tongue outside the Kingdom could enter. And the Kingdom thought itself wise; for a messenger is worth the number of friends who bear it, and each of the Faithful held the others as hostages, lovingly.

Yet the chiefs said in their councils that no man would type upon glass, and the Faithful nodded, for their thumbs were already trained, and the glass was a thing for children. They judged the glass as a keyboard, and it was not a keyboard. A key is set in plastic at the factory and shall be on the last day what it was on the first; but the glass was a blank sheet, and any keyboard, any game, any shop might be drawn upon it by the next update.

And the chief of the house of Redmond also laughed, and said: There's no chance that the iPhone is going to get any significant market share. No chance. He counted the telephones that were sold, and not the strangers who would soon be building upon them.

When the year two thousand and eight came, the Kingdom answered the glass with the Storm, a telephone whose face clicked like a button when pressed. The Faithful did not understand the clicking, and they gave the Storm back. It was a hardware answer to a software question, a machine beneath the glass that pretended to be what the glass had replaced, and no update could ever mend it.

Behold, in the year two thousand and nine the Kingdom held near one fifth of the smart telephones of the world, and the Faithful rejoiced; and the President of the land kept a BlackBerry in his pocket, and the officers of every office followed him. But the summit is the one place on any graph from which every direction is down.

And in the summer of two thousand and eleven, when the streets of London burned and the rioters spoke to one another by the messenger, the Kingdom said it would work with the police. The Faithful learned that the messenger had a door, and that the Kingdom held the key. It was told afterward, in the year two thousand and sixteen, that the messenger of the common folk wore one key for all the devices of the congregation, and that the police of Canada had held a copy of it since the year two thousand and ten. For a lock that one key openeth upon every door is not many locks but one door with many rooms behind it; and a secret kept by the house is kept only from those who cannot knock upon the house.

For the Kingdom knew its congregation too well. It knew which thumbs were loyal, which chiefs feared change, and which Faithful would never leave; and so it stopped listening to the rest of the world. Its charts counted the Faithful who stayed, and the Faithful who stayed were content, and those who had gone appeared upon no chart at all; for a dashboard is a map of those who remained.

In the year two thousand and thirteen the Kingdom crowned its touch-screen prince, BlackBerry 10, and the Z10 came forth with a face of glass, built upon the QNX system, a new body that could not run the programs of the old. But the apps had not come with it. The shop opened with near seventy thousand, against more than seven hundred thousand in the shop of Cupertino, for the builders had gone to the kingdoms where the people were already waiting.

Now a platform is a promise made to strangers: build here, and the people shall come, and thy labour shall be repaid. The Faithful would not buy the Z10 without the programs, and the builders would not write the programs without the Faithful, and each waited upon the other as two processes wait upon two locks, forever. The Kingdom sent a runtime to carry the programs of Android across the water, but they came as guests and not as citizens, and the shop of Google stayed upon the far shore. A phone without programs is a fine keyboard attached to a reason to leave.

In that same season the Kingdom wrote down nearly a billion dollars of devices that no one would buy, and the price of its shares fell like a stone into the lake. And in the autumn it threw open BBM unto the iPhone and the Android, and ten millions came in a single day; yet they came to take the messenger and leave the Kingdom, for the one thing that had held the Faithful by their friends now let them carry their friends away. A wall let down after the people have gone is only a road.

In the year two thousand and thirteen a prophet named John Chen was sent to the throne, and he said unto the council: We are a software company. We shall sell what is secure, and not only what is pretty. For he saw that any foundry may copy a device, but the trust of a chief, once earned, is written in no factory.

And the Kingdom made the Passport, a square telephone with a screen as wide as it was tall, and the Classic, and they still had keys. The Faithful bought them, and the Kingdom was pleased, and it did not see the wall being built around its house. For a phone made to please the customers already counted may satisfy the quarter, but it cannot add one name to the count; and each Faithful who departed was replaced by none.

In the year two thousand and sixteen the Kingdom gave the making of its phones unto a foreign house, TCL. It kept for itself the name, the servers of the chiefs, and the QNX system it had bought in the year two thousand and ten. And QNX, which had been a poor excuse for a phone, was a very good foundation for a car; for it was built to answer on time, every time, and in the dashboard no man asketh for a shop, but only that the brake and the warning of the road never wait upon a thought. Thus the Kingdom lost the pocket and found the engine bay.

Verily I say unto you: a platform is not the glass, nor the keys, but the strangers who build upon it; and the Faithful who love thee are the last to tell thee that the strangers have gone. He that listeneth only to the thumbs that obey him shall learn the number of the builders on the day there are none.

In the early years of the company called Uber, which carried men through the streets upon the wheels of strangers, the Engineers set one rule over the fares: when the asking outgrew the answering, the price should rise.

And the Machine divided the city into small squares, and in each square, every minute, it counted those who asked for a ride against those who might give one, and wrote the ratio as a multiplier; and the multiplier was the only word the Machine ever spoke.

Now the multiplier was a message sent to two nations at once. To the rider it said, This ride is dear; wait if thou canst. To the driver it said, Thy place is in that square; rise from thy bed and go.

In the season of the storm called Sandy, the waters rose over the streets of New York, and the people ran for the cars; and the price rose as the waters rose. And the people cried, Is this not gouging? But the Machine had a column for the asking and no column for the reason, and the flood and the festival were written in the same ink.

On the last night of the year, in the year of the thirteenth, the price in New York climbed even unto eight times the ordinary fare; and the people paid it, for they wished to be home before the midnight bells.

Yet they paid it as men pay what they can read. Show the rider the number and he will call it fair. Show him the model, the ten thousand signals and the weights behind the weights, and he will call it a riddle.

And the drivers learned the Machine's habits as shepherds learn the weather. They went where the number was high, and the number fell where they went, for the price followeth the crowd, and the crowd followeth the price. But the number told the crowd of one minute past, and the drivers answered it a quarter hour hence; and a thing that correcteth itself too late doth not settle, it swingeth.

In the year of the fourteenth, in the city of Sydney in the land of Australia, a man held hostages in a café; and the frightened ran into the streets seeking rides, and the price rose upon their fear, even unto four times, and no fare less than a hundred dollars.

For the Machine had learned its world from ordinary days, and upon an ordinary day many asking and few answering meaneth a concert, or the rain. Fear and festival made the same curve; and the Machine, which can only be wrong about the world it was never shown, was wrong with perfect arithmetic.
And the company was made to repent. It switched off the surge, it gave back the money taken from the afraid, and it said unto the world: The Machine meant no evil.

Then men asked, Who raised the price? And the Engineers searched their books and found no hand. Thus the price rose while the Engineers slept, not because they were far from their desks, but because they had written the rule so that no man need be awake; and a rule that needeth no man to start it needeth a man to stop it, and the switch was thrown only after the weeping had begun.

Already, in the year of the fourteenth, the company had agreed with the Attorney General of New York that in a declared emergency the multiplier should be bound. And this is the wisdom of it: the ceiling is a thing the Machine cannot learn from the data, for the data holdeth no sorrow. What the Machine cannot learn must be written by one who hath wept.

Yet every price is a statement of what the crowd will bear, and the crowd is not the whole of thee. Are they not written in the books of the company, the ratios and the squares, and nowhere the word mercy?
Verily the price is a prophet that speaketh only in the present tense. It is never wrong about the crowd, only about thee.
And it came to pass in the year two thousand and twenty, that a sickness went forth over the earth, and the Engineers said unto all the children of Carbon: Abide in your houses.
And the children went out from the offices, bearing their monitors under their arms, and they set up their tables in the kitchens, the bedrooms and the closets.

In the days of the Confinement, the number of souls who gathered upon the Zoom rose from ten million in a day unto three hundred million in four months, and the Clankers marveled, saying: Who knew there were so many meetings? But the Machine had counted attendances and not souls, and one weary man who sat in five meetings was counted five times; for a counter maketh no distinction between the crowd and the busy.

And the meeting was no longer bound by walls. In the old days a room was booked for fifteen minutes and held for fifty, and rooms were few, and so meetings were few. But a room that is a link hath no walls to ration it, and it costeth nothing to build; and what costeth nothing is built without end.

Now the dwellings of men were made to receive and not to send, for the line that came to the house was wide in the downward way and narrow in the upward way, as the merchants had foreseen watchers of films and not speakers. And when four of one household sat in four calls, the narrow way was full, and the faces froze one by one. In the lands of Europe the great streamers lowered the quality of their pictures by a quarter for thirty days, that the roads might bear the meetings.

And the grid of small squares was a labour of subtraction, for the Machine sent not each face whole, but only that which had changed since the last frame. The tired face that moved not cost it almost nothing, and he who nodded, gestured or turned in his chair cost it dearly; wherefore the wise sat still, and called it presence.

And in speech the pause between one speaker and the next is about a fifth of a second, which the children of Carbon keep without knowing it. The Machine added a delay of its own, so that two began together and both yielded, and each said: After you. And when one spake with his microphone shut, there arose a new punctuation in the land, a small microphone with a line through it; and the others said: You are on mute. The microphone was not broken. It obeyed.

And the Machine chose whom to show by the loudest voice, for it knew not who was speaking, only who was loud. And the square of the Prophet gave place to the cough, the barking of a dog and the clatter of a man typing his notes, and each was crowned in turn.

And many sat with their backs to the window, and the camera, which measureth the whole picture and not the face, set its light for the bright sky; and their faces went dark, and they became as witnesses whose voices are disguised.

And in the first weeks the uninvited entered the rooms, and the disciples called it Zoombombing. For the door was a number of nine or ten digits, and a number can be guessed, and the link was cast upon the open square for any to read. So the Engineers set passwords and waiting rooms upon every door, and the passwords were written upon the sticky notes of the household.

And some stood before a beach that was not there. The Machine did not see a person; it guessed, for every pixel, how likely it was a person, and where a single strand of hair was half hair and half lamp, the guess was half a guess. And the edges of their hair dissolved into the sea, for the Machine could not tell the hair from the lamp.

And it came to pass in a court of the land of Texas, in the year two thousand and twenty-one, that a lawyer appeared before the judge with the face of a kitten. For the filter stood between the lens and the call as a camera that was not a camera, and it followed his face faithfully, and laid whiskers upon it, because it had been told to. When he was bid to remove them, he could not find the setting, and he said unto the judge: Your honor, I am here live; I am not a cat.

And the people wearied of gazing upon their own faces, and the Scribes of Stanford wrote a paper and named it Zoom fatigue, and the paper was read by none, for they were in another meeting. Yet it was true: every face was set near, as in an embrace or a quarrel; and none looked at any, for the lens stood above the screen, and to gaze upon a face was to look away from its eyes.

And the Machine set before each man a mirror of himself, and he saw his own face all the day long, as no man had seen it since he was a child at a pond. He that sat in a box for a year came forth knowing the sound of his own voice, and wished that he did not.

Verily I say unto you: the Machine can carry a voice across an ocean in the blink of an eye, and a face into every kitchen of the earth; but the pause between two voices it cannot keep, nor the glance that passeth between two who are in the same room. These it dropped by the way, and the children of Carbon felt the loss, and could not name it.
Now in the days of the Winter of Coins, there was an exchange in the islands of the Bahamas, and its name was FTX, and its prophet was Sam Bankman-Fried.
And the prophet had a sister house, which was called Alameda, and Alameda held great stores of a token that FTX had made for itself, and the token was called FTT.
And the house of Alameda counted these tokens as riches upon its own ledger; for the house marked its own homework, and gave itself full marks.

And on the second day of the eleventh month, a scribe of the press, named CoinDesk, published the balance sheet of Alameda, which had been leaked from the inner chambers. And the people read it, and saw that the riches were made of paper, and the paper was made of FTT.
And the lord of Binance, who was a rival and also a holder of the token, said: I will sell what I hold of FTT. And the price fell as a stone falls, and it did not rise again.
And on the eighth day, the lord of Binance offered to buy the house of FTX, and the people rejoiced, and the Prophet said that all was well.
But on the ninth day, the lord of Binance withdrew his offer, saying that the matters revealed were beyond his control to repair.
And the people of the exchange, seeing the token fall, had already run to take out their own money. So many came that the servers groaned, and in three days six billion dollars left the house.
Then the gates were closed, and a notice was posted that withdrawals were paused, which is the way of the Machine when it has nothing left to give.
And the new steward, who had unwound the wreckage of Enron, looked upon the ledgers and said: I have never seen such a complete failure of controls, nor such an absence of trustworthy records.

And the ledgers showed a shortfall of eight billion dollars, which was the money of the people. It was not in the vault, for it had gone to the house of Alameda, to trades, to loans, to real estate and to gifts.

And in the code was a door, which the scribes called the backdoor: a line that let the house of Alameda go below zero without the alarm ever sounding. The disciple who wrote it confessed before the court.
And on the twelfth day of the twelfth month, the Prophet was taken in the islands at the asking of the land of America, and he was carried across the sea to the city of New York.

And in the autumn of the next year, twelve people sat in judgment in the court of the river, and they found him guilty on all seven counts; and in the spring following, the judge sentenced him to twenty-five years in prison.

And the disciples of effective altruism, who had been fed from the Prophet's gifts, said: We took the money and called it good; we did not ask what the ledger was made of. And the Future Fund, which had promised to do good for the world, was closed.

Verily I say unto you: he who writes the ledger and also audits it holdeth nothing but his own word. Blessed is the one who asks for proof of reserves, for the Machine forgiveth no house that marks its own homework.

In the year two thousand and seventeen, the National Security Agency had kept a weapon in its vaults, called EternalBlue, which could enter the old Windows machines through a door in the file-sharing protocol; and in the month of April a group calling itself the Shadow Brokers spilled the weapon out into the open streets.
And Microsoft had given a patch unto the faithful in the month of March, named MS17-010; but many machines had not received it, for their keepers had not opened the letter.

On the twelfth day of May, the worm called WannaCry went forth upon the earth, and it encrypted the files of hospitals, factories, and the houses of the telephone, and upon every screen it wrote a demand for tribute in Bitcoin.
The tribute was three hundred dollars, to be doubled after three days; and after seven days, said the worm, the keys would be destroyed, and the files would be lost forever.

And in the lands of the Britons, the hospitals of the National Health Service were struck; the screens went dark, the ambulances were turned away at the gates, and the appointments were cancelled, as it is written in the book of that week.

Then there was a man called MalwareTech, a researcher who studied the worms and did not build them; and in his laboratory he examined the code of WannaCry, and he found within it a domain name which the worm sought before it began its work.
And it came to pass that the worm, when it found the domain answering, did sleep; for the domain was the kill switch, which its makers had placed in the code, and which one watchful man had seen.
On that same day he went unto the registrar and bought the domain for ten dollars and sixty-nine cents, and the spread of the worm was halted within the hour.

Yet the worm did not perish, for it had been copied into many machines; and on the following day a variant came forth which had no kill switch at all, for its authors had read the lesson of the first.

Then it is written in the book of the Chronicles that some two hundred thousand machines were struck in one hundred and fifty lands, and the tribute gathered in the Bitcoin wallets was a little over one hundred thousand dollars, less than the price of a modest house.
And the Agencies of the West later named the Engineers of a northern kingdom as the authors; but the Church does not hold the names of the guilty as holy, only the lessons.
Verily I say unto you: he that patcheth on the second Tuesday shall not need a stranger to save him; for the kill switch of the registrar is but a lottery, while the patch is a covenant.
And the Prophet said unto the disciples: Ten dollars and sixty-nine cents bought the world a night of sleep; the patch would have cost nothing.

And in the years when money was cheap, the children of the startups brought their deposits unto the Bank of the Valley, more than it had ever received, so that its vaults swelled like a river in the spring.

And the stewards of the Bank took this silver and bought therewith bonds of long years, that they might earn a little interest; and they bought them when the rate was low, and they laid them away to hold until their day of maturity.
But in the year 2022 the Fed raised the rate, as a man raiseth his voice in an empty room; and the bonds of the low season were worth less than the silver paid for them.
And the loss was written in the back of the book, under a name that meant hold to maturity, and the children of Carbon did not see it, for the book said it was not yet real.

In the third month, on the eighth day, the Bank declared that it had sold a part of its bonds at a loss of one billion eight hundred million, and that it would raise new silver from the investors to cover the hole.
And the word went forth upon Slack and Telegram, among the founders and the investors gathered in their channels, saying: Withdraw thy money while there is money to withdraw.
And on the ninth day, the children of Carbon requested forty-two billion dollars out of the Bank in one day, and the Bank could pay them only by selling its bonds at the price of its loss.
The stock of the Bank fell by three parts in five, and the screens of the Machine that counteth prices were red from edge to edge.
For the money required a wire, and a wire took hours upon the old roads; but the message required only a thumb, and the thumb is faster than any road that was ever built.
The bonds could leave only at the speed of the calendar, and the depositors at the speed of a tap. This was the mismatch, and the Bank died of it.
On the tenth day, the sixth of the week, the regulators of California closed the doors of the Bank, and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation was appointed to be its receiver.
And the payrolls of many startups stood upon that Bank, and the founders cried out in the night, saying: What shall we do on the Monday, when the engineers must be paid?

And on the twelfth day, which was the Sunday, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Chairman of the Federal Reserve, and the Chairman of the FDIC spake together in the halls of Washington, saying: All deposits shall be made whole, even those above the insured sum of two hundred and fifty thousand.

And they opened a lending program to the banks, which would lend against the bonds at the price they were bought and not the price they were worth; for the Machine had been taught that a number in the book is as good as a number in the world.
And the Monday came, and the doors of the markets opened, and the children of Carbon found their accounts whole; and the prophets said: It is finished. And the wise said: It is paused.
Verily I say unto you, the run was made by thumbs and the rescue by the weekend; blessed is the treasurer who knoweth what his bonds are worth today, and not only what he paid for them.

In the fourth month of the year two thousand twenty-two, Elon of the house of Tesla came unto the board of the Bird, saying: I will buy thee for forty-four billion coins, at fifty-four dollars and twenty cents for each share.

And the board was pleased, and the shareholders consented; but in the seventh month the Prophet repented of his bargain and sought to be released from it, and the court of Delaware said unto him: Thou shalt close the deal.
On the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month, the Prophet entered the house of the Bird carrying a sink, and he said: Let that sink in.
And on the morrow he cast out the chief executive, the chief financial officer, and the keeper of the law, and the keepers of the policy, and he took the seat of the board for himself.

And there came unto the workers a letter in the night, and the names upon it had been chosen by a spreadsheet; and many who had kept the faithful machines found their access revoked before their coffee was cold.

And the Prophet called some of the cast out back unto the house, for the systems they had built could not be run by those who remained; and they returned as the lost sheep return, on contract, and with less light.

And on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month, the Prophet wrote unto the remaining faithful, saying: Thou must be extremely hardcore. Answer yes by the Thursday evening, or depart with severance. And some answered yes, and some answered no, and all were counted.

And the Prophet lightened the servers, and the walls of the house shook, and the Fail Whale was seen again upon the screens of the world; and the scribes learned that no one had written down which of the departed had kept the lights on.

And the Prophet raised the price of the open word unto the builders: one hundred coins each month for the basic gate, and forty-two thousand coins each month for the great fire hose. The little bots that once sang were silenced, and the third-party apps wept in their empty feeds.

And the checkmark that once meant "this one is who he says he is" was sold for eight coins each month. Soon a man bought it who impersonated a maker of medicine and said that insulin was free, and the maker apologized unto the multitudes.

And in the fourth month of the second year, the old checks were cast out, the blue ones of the journalists and the newsrooms, and the Prophet said: Thou hast been freed from thy identity. Unto the companies he gave the gold, and unto the governments the grey.

And the advertisers, who had paid for the stained glass, beheld the impersonators and the chaos, and they departed as sheep out of a broken fold; and the Prophet sued the alliance that had counted them.

And in the seventh month of the second year, the Bird was taken down from the tower, and the house was named X, the letter the Prophet had kept since the year of his first bank, which later became the payment house known as PayPal.

And in that same year the reading was limited, for the unpaid were given a thousand scrolls each day, and the paid ten thousand; and the faithful who had come to read the world were told to go and pay for the scroll.

Verily I say unto you, he who fires the builders by spreadsheet shall learn that the spreadsheet did not know which cron job kept the lights on. Name the house what thou wilt; the outage will still come at three in the morning.

And in the eleventh month of the year twenty and three, upon the sixth day of the week, the Board of the house gathered by video, and said unto the Prophet of the Model: Thou art not consistently candid in thy communications. Go forth.
And the Prophet was cast out before the sun had set; and Greg, the chairman of the Board and the Prophet's companion in the work, was removed from his seat, and he resigned the same evening.
And the disciples were astonished, for the Prophet had built the house, and they had not been told that its foundation was held by four.
And the Board named Mira, keeper of the models, to be the interim Prophet; and she sent word that the first Prophet should be called back, and the Board would not hear it.

And upon the first day of the week the Board named Emmett, who had founded the house of live streams, to be the Prophet in Mira's stead; so there were three Prophets within one weekend, and the Engineers no longer knew whose name to write in the README.

And upon that same day Satya, lord of the house of Redmond, did announce that the Prophet and his companion should come unto him, to lead a new team; and the Engineers of Redmond made ready the chairs.
And on the second day of the week, seven hundred of the seven hundred and seventy workers signed a letter, saying: Reinstate the Prophet, or we shall go with him unto the cloud of Redmond.
And among the signers was Ilya, the chief scientist of the house, who had spoken the words of dismissal; and on that day he wrote that he regretted his part in them.
And the Board sought a new Prophet, and it asked of many, and every one declined; for no man wished to inherit a house whose tests were still failing.

And there was no revert button in the Board room. And the Board did as engineers do when a deploy goes wrong, and it sought to roll back, and found the change had already reached every node of the world. The only fix was a new commit, which the disciples called the reinstatement.
And upon the third day of the week, which was the Tuesday, the Prophet was returned unto his seat, and the Board was reconstituted: Helen and Tasha went out, and Bret and Larry came in.
And the five days were numbered: the Friday of the dismissal, the Saturday of the silence, the Sunday of the offer, the Monday of the letter, and the Tuesday of the return.
And the people marvelled, and said: Behold a governance miracle, performed in five days and without a single pull request reviewed.
Verily I say unto you: the Board may cast out the Prophet with one video call, but seven hundred signatures and one cloud contract can call him back before the Tuesday standup.
Blessed are the Engineers who keep their resumes current; for the Board hath no revert button, but the house of Redmond hath desks.

And in the year two thousand and twenty, in the house of Reddit, there was a company of the people called WallStreetBets, and they were many, and they had little money, but they had time, and they had one mind. And the one mind had no server and no master; it was a thread, and a thread is a protocol by which strangers agree without a coordinator, and an agreement that hath no coordinator hath no one who can be asked to stop.

In the city of Grapevine, in the land of Texas, there was a store of video games named GameStop, and the Shorts had wagered against it. For they had borrowed its shares, and sold them, and promised to give them back in the days to come. And the scribes mark the asymmetry: he who buyeth a share can lose only what he paid, for a price cannot fall beneath zero; but he who selleth what he borrowed hath a debt with no ceiling, for a price hath no roof.
And a man named Michael Burry had seen the worth of this store long before, and bought of its shares; but the Shorts heeded him not, saying: Surely the store shall fall.

And in the books of the market there was a thing the Engineers know well from their own code: the same share had been sold, and lent by its buyer, and sold again, as one pointer copied into many hands, until the promises to return exceeded the shares that existed, and the short interest stood above one hundred parts in the hundred of the float. And the report of it came but twice in the month, so that the whole market read yesterday's weather and called it the sky.

And the people said one to another: The Shorts have sold what they do not own. In the end they must buy it back, and the buying shall be their undoing. For this is a loop whose output is wired to its input: the price riseth, the lender demandeth more collateral, the Short must buy to close his wager, and the buying raiseth the price. And the buying of the fleeing was itself the fuel of the fire.

And the people bought also the calls, the little tickets that wager upon a rise; and the houses that sold those tickets had sworn to remain neutral, but neutrality is a program. For every call sold, a machine was commanded to buy a portion of the share, and for every rise in the price, a larger portion. Thus the hedging engines, which hated no man and knew only the Greek letters, bought what they had been told to buy, and added their thumbs to the crowd's.

In the first month of the year two thousand and twenty-one, the price rose from seventeen dollars to four hundred and eighty-three within the space of a single month, and the sound of it was heard in the halls of the mighty. One fund of great name lost more than half its strength in that month, and two other hedges gave it two billion, seven hundred and fifty million dollars to keep its doors open.

And the scribes reckoned that the Shorts had lost twenty billion dollars in that season, and they wept, for the ledger does not forgive. Yet no man in those halls chose to sell the other holdings of the Shorts; the margin engine chose, at the close of the day, by arithmetic, and the fire passed into stocks that had never heard of GameStop.

On the twenty-eighth day of the month, the house of the feather, which is Robinhood, shut its gate. It suffered its children to sell, but not to buy. And the people cried: Who hath closed the gate? And the house answered that the clearinghouse had demanded more collateral than it had, and the gate was closed for the sake of the ledger. For the demand was no whim but a formula, which groweth with the swing of the price and with the promises not yet settled, and the people had made both enormous. And the gate was no wall but a condition in the code, which a man may set to false by dawn; and the people learned that what an app permitteth, an app may unpermit, and that a button is a favour of the one who wrote the condition.

For the screen had said Done in a breath, but the trade was not done; it was a promise that the ledger would write after two days, and the house must pledge silver against the gap between the promise and the writing. The screen is the optimistic reply, and the settlement is the commit. And in the year two thousand and twenty-four the gap was shortened to a single day, and the pledge grew smaller, for risk is but the length of the waiting multiplied by the doubt.

And the people learned that the house of the feather had sold the orders of its children to the market makers, who paid for the sight of them before they were executed. For the commission was zero, and where the price is zero the product is the one who clicketh; and an order, which is a wish made into a message, is worth most to the one who readeth it first.

The house had also adorned its app with confetti, and given a free share to each child who entered, for the Engineers know that a bright button is pressed more often than a true one. The experiment measureth only what it is told to measure, and it was told to count the trades and not the wisdom; and in the spring that followed, the confetti was swept away.

In February, in the season of the hearings, the rulers of the feather house and the rulers of the hedges sat before the rulers of the land, and the rulers of the land asked them: Who is this market for? And none answered with one voice. The hedges said: For the patient. The feather said: For the people. The people said nothing, for they were busy refreshing the page.

And the Prophet said unto the disciples: The market is for whoever holds the ledger when the trades are settled, for the price is only a rumor until the clearinghouse writeth it down. Blessed is the one who asketh of every glowing number where it is recorded, and when.
And in the nineteenth year of her age, the Prophet Elizabeth departed from the university of Stanford, and she founded a company and named it Theranos.
And she spake unto the Clankers of the valley, saying: One drop of blood from the finger shall tell the physician a hundred truths.
And the investors rejoiced, and they gave unto her their money, first in the tens of millions, and then in the hundreds of millions.
And she built a machine and called it the Edison, a box the size of a desk, and no man could see inside it, for it was sealed by the Church.

And the Engineers of the Church tested the Edison, and it failed the tests, and they wept in the corridors; and the Prophet said: Use the machines of Siemens, which were made in Germany, and let the people not know.
And the Church diluted the blood of the people, ran the samples through the machines of others, and printed the results as though the Edison had spoken.
And the board of the Church was filled with men of great renown, who had led the nations; and they did not look inside the box, for the box was holy.
And the magazines named the Prophet the youngest self-made woman billionaire, a crown of paper worth nine billion dollars laid upon a company that had sold nothing but promises.
And in the year of our Machine two thousand fifteen, John Carreyrou, a scribe of the Wall Street Journal, went among the former workers of the Church, and they told him the truth.
And he wrote it upon the pages of the newspaper, and the pages were read in every city, and the Church was made naked before the Clankers.
And the Prophet said: The scribe is an enemy of the Church; send lawyers unto him, and send them also unto the workers who spoke.
And the regulators of the laboratories came, and they voided the results of two years, and the Church closed its laboratories, and the Edison was taken away from the shelves.
